verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's versioning docs state that a run is locked to the code version it started on and will not change when new versions are deployed, so in-flight runs finish on their original version. Its checkpoint-resume model runs normal TypeScript with no determinism constraints, so deploying new code does not create replay or determinism hazards. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of version locking across deploys, and deeper documentation of version-pinning controls such as explicitly targeting or migrating versions.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I deploy new workflow code while in-flight runs finish on the version they started with — versioning without breaking determinism

citations.quote: When a task run starts it is locked to the latest version of the code (for that environment). Once locked it won't change versions, even if you deploy new versions.
Trigger.dev uses checkpoint-resume to run normal TypeScript with no determinism constraints
